subject: Competitive eval follow-up & next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Liu <alex.liu@acme.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.inference, aditya.rao@redwood.inference
Date: Tue, 25 Feb 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: competitive eval & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call summary:
- Use case: product QA and customer support autopilot for Acme Core (high accuracy, low hallucination).
- Current stack: experimenting with Bedrock and OpenAI; primary evaluation metrics are factual accuracy on internal QA set, hallucination rate, and 95th percentile latency under 8k tokens.
- Ask: a short competitive evaluation comparing Redwood "redwood-base-1" (quantized) vs Bedrock/Vertex/OpenAI on your eval prompts.

Key differentiators we promised to validate:
- Latency & throughput at 2–8k sequence lengths (continuous batching benefits).
- Hallucination rate on product QA prompts (we often see different hallucination failure modes vs large closed models).
- Cost per QA transaction after batching/prefix caching.

Proposed next tests (simple, fast):
1) Run the attached eval_prompt_set_v1.txt (60 prompts) across: redwood-base-1, openai-gpt-4o, aws-bedrock-1.
2) Measure: exact-match/answer-type accuracy, hallucination flag (binary), and 95p latency.
3) Share results in the CSV template attached (evaluation_results_template.csv).
4) If you want, we can also spin up a short Dedicated trial (2 GPU hours) so you can test with your real dataset in a private environment — requires a quick SOW.

Attachments: eval_prompt_set_v1.txt and evaluation_results_template.csv (simple CSV for result import).

Next steps I propose:
- You share a sample of 200 product QA examples (anonymized) by EOD Friday so we can run a full pass next week.
- We schedule a 30-min follow-up on Mon Mar 1 to review results and discuss any regression tests.

If procurement or security needs context, I can loop in our security lead.

Thanks — looking forward to the test run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Internal notes: procurement (procurement@acme.com) is looped for timeline/PO. A few quick answers and asks: 

1) Timeline: we should be able to share the 200-sample set by Thursday (2026-03-04).
2) Security: Can you confirm SOC 2 Type II in-scope and whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/private setups? Procurement asked for a quick statement they can include in the SOW.
3) For the test, please run your eval against our samples and include the hallucination flag so we can compare perimeter drift.

We’d also like to include a brief demo showing throughput improvements with batching if you have a short recording or a 15-min live demo slot. Does Mon Mar 1 at 2:00pm PT work?

On the demo scheduling — happy to confirm once I hear back on SOC2/KMS.

Thanks,
Alex
Product Lead — Acme Retail
alex.liu@acme.com

Hi Alex —

Short answers for procurement/security: 
- SOC 2 Type II: yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified. Attached is a recent snapshot for procurement review (SOC2-snapshot.pdf).
- Customer-managed KMS: supported in our Dedicated and Private offerings; for Hosted we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest in some configurations — we can scope in the SOW.

We can definitely demo batching/throughput. I’m available Mon Mar 1 at 2:00pm PT; I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Regarding the eval harness: I’ve provisioned a shared drive with the evaluation template and a quick runbook (link below). If you can drop the anonymized 200 samples there we’ll queue the run and share results in the CSV.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-eval-link

Attachments: SOC2-snapshot.pdf

I’ll also loop in Aditya (cc’d) to align on the exact prompt set and regression checks we’ll run.

Best,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, dev.patel@redwood.inference
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan: prompts & regression checks

Marissa / Dev —

Quick technical plan for the run once Acme drops the 200 samples: 

1) Prompt sets: we’ll use eval_prompt_set_v1.txt as agreed for the initial pass, then run eval_prompts_v2.jsonl (covers edge-case hallucination prompts and multi-turn QA) for regression checks if we see variance.
2) Models: redwood-base-1 (quantized, our recommended config), openai-gpt-4o (api), aws-bedrock (gpt-like variant). We’ll pin sequence lengths to 2k and 6k to capture latency at both ranges.
3) Metrics: exact-match, F1 (where applicable), hallucination_rate (we’ll flag answers that reference non-existent product features), and a hallucination_reason short tag (e.g., ‘fabricated_entity’, ‘unsupported_inference’).
4) Regression checks: run pairwise diff between redwood-base-1 (baseline) and other models; create a list of top 10 prompts where hallucination increased compared to baseline.
5) Output: populate evaluation_results_template.csv and include a short JSONL with per-example model outputs for manual inspection (we’ll redact PII).

Operational notes: 
- We’ll run tests in our hosted environment first; if Acme prefers Dedicated (for KMS/data residency), we can mirror the run there — note that dedicated setup takes ~48hrs to provision.
- Cost estimate for the run (hosted): ~$120 in compute (will confirm after run).

I’ll prepare the runner and a short script (run_eval.sh) that you can run locally if needed.

Aditya
Sr. Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.inference
